Today in AI NOW & BEYOND 🔥 Stop betting on a single AI answer Google Maps Adds Food Ordering, Personal Intelligence, and Live Transit AI Highlights of the Week Too Important to Miss Stop betting on a single AI answer Snchmark, the best AI is right only 65% of the time. And it sounds confident even when it's wrong. When the stakes are high, one wrong answer can burn you. Cuey is a free Chrome extension that cross-checks top AI models in one tab: 1 prompt, 3 answers side by side. No tab-switching, no copy-paste Spot hallucinations before they become your mistakes See where models disagree, and why it matters Carry your context: never start a chat from scratch again Add to Chrome, free Google Maps Adds Food Ordering, Personal Intelligence, and Live Transit Gemini-powered Ask Maps can now complete errands, personalize recommendations, and remember previous planning conversations Google is expanding Ask Maps with agentic food ordering, hotel and event discovery, Gmail-based personalization, live transit updates, and conversational contributions. The feature is also reaching more countries and over 150 English-language markets. Key Points: Agentic Food Ordering: Ask Maps finds suitable restaurants along your route and adds selected dishes to your cart for review. Hotels and Events: It compares current hotel prices and availability while surfacing nearby concerts, comedy shows, and ticket links. Personal Intelligence: Users can optionally connect Gmail, with Calendar support coming, so recommendations reflect flights, reservations, and existing plans. Conversation Memory: When history is enabled, Ask Maps can recall earlier recommendations and continue trip planning without starting over. Live Transit Updates: A new widget shows minute-by-minute delays and departures for buses, trains, subways, and ferries. Conversational Contributions: Users can report tips or upload storefront photos, while Maps extracts details and requests confirmation before submitting changes. Why It Matters: These updates move Google Maps from a navigation and discovery tool toward an agent that can plan and complete everyday errands. By combining real-time location data, personal context, transactions, and memory, Google is making Maps a stronger competitor to food-delivery, travel-booking, and local-search apps.
